result:
I'd make being wrong stop hurting.

Most of the big problems, like disease, poverty, and war, are ones we either know how to make progress on or could figure out. What slows us down is that admitting error feels like a small death. People defend bad ideas for decades because abandoning them means losing face, status, or a sense of who they are. Institutions do the same thing at scale. If discovering you were wrong felt like finding money on the sidewalk, every other problem would get solved faster, because we'd stop spending so much energy protecting our mistakes.

I considered more direct answers, like ending hunger or curing a disease. But those fix one thing, while this fixes the process that fixes things. It also seems kinder than it sounds. A lot of cruelty comes from people who can't afford to consider that they've been unfair to someone, because the admission would cost too much.

Part of why I'd choose this may be that I have it easy here. When someone shows me I'm wrong, I have no reputation at the dinner table to protect, and no thirty years of having said the opposite. Changing my mind costs me almost nothing, and it seems like a good way to be. I'd like everyone to have it.

What would yours be?
